what: blaze-usercode Given::env_keyed (crates/blaze-usercode/src/lib.rs) hashes a proc-macro call crate variables with about 80 Hasher::part calls (each a tiny update through one-block compressions): about 2.3 us for 40 variables, 3 KB, against 0.5 us at BLAKE3 SIMD rate, so a proc-macro hit is 23% over its bound (docs/v2/plan/lanes/usercode/speed-of-light-macros.md, A hit). Change: gather the length-prefixed names and values into an 8 KiB stack buffer and give BLAKE3 the whole buffer, as trace::Keyer does for index::find, keeping the same bytes hashed (a test against per-piece updates). The sort of the 40 pairs (0.9 us) goes too if base_db::Env hands them out in name order.

history.note: crates/blaze-usercode/src/lib.rs: Given::env_keyed gathers the length-prefixed names and values into an 8 KiB stack batch (struct Batched) and hands BLAKE3 the whole batch; the same bytes are hashed. Test keyed_variables_batched_hash_as_one_part_each checks it against one Hasher::part per piece, across the batch end and past its size. The sort is stable (driftsort), so names already in order cost n-1 comparisons.
